# CountryEvent()

> **CountryEvent**&lt;`Id` *extends* `string`&gt;(`spec`: [`EventSpec`](../interfaces/EventSpec.md)&lt;[`CountryScope`](../interfaces/CountryScope.md)&gt; & `object`): [`EventDefinition`](../interfaces/EventDefinition.md)&lt;`"country"`, `Id`&gt;

Defined in: [src/sdk/index.ts:245](https://github.com/maxmixalex/krieg-lang/blob/main/src/sdk/index.ts#L245)

Declare a country event and return its typed handle. Keep the handle when scheduling from another definition: TypeScript checks the receiver scope and preserves the literal event ID.

## Type Parameters

| Type Parameter |
| ------ |
| <a id="type-parameter-id"></a> `Id` *extends* `string` |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `spec` | [`EventSpec`](../interfaces/EventSpec.md)&lt;[`CountryScope`](../interfaces/CountryScope.md)&gt; & `object` |

## Returns

[`EventDefinition`](../interfaces/EventDefinition.md)&lt;`"country"`, `Id`&gt;

## Example

```ts
const grant = CountryEvent({
  id: "council.001", hidden: true, isTriggeredOnly: true,
  immediate: country => country.effects.addPoliticalPower(10),
});
// In a country effect callback: country.schedule(grant, { days: 2 }).
```
